chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb ibn Ya'qub from Abu Basir said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man to whom the dowry of a woman is entrusted, and he deducts it from the dowry of his wives, so he said: 'It is attached to the dowry of his wives.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man uses a woman's entrusted dowry to pay for the dowries of his other wives?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial liability when a man, entrusted with a specific woman's dowry, deducts from it to pay the dowries of his other wives. The ruling establishes that the deducted amount is legally attached to the obligations of those other wives, ensuring their dowry rights are preserved despite the source of funds. This highlights the precision in Shia jurisprudence regarding *mahr* (dowry) distribution and the concept of *wilayah* (trusteeship) in marital finances.
